title: Native B70 single-flight provider lifecycle

sources.notes: Build graph for the low-level NVFP4 harness, public provider API harness and stdin control executable; links embedded QuixiCore-XPU. It has no language symbol and does not build b70_provider_int4_chain_test.cpp.
Public lifecycle/status/capability ABI, single-flight issue/take contract, output-wire publication requirement, host-range ownership, memory query, command-streamer alternatives and shutdown.

Primary modeled implementation. Exact bank parsing, device selection, persistent ownership, classic single flight, kernel-branch selection, copyout publication, async poison, fail-open telemetry, native queue latches and ordered teardown are modeled; device arithmetic and raw command encoding are explicit external abstractions.

Standalone capability/health/shutdown control surface. It does not expose issue/take and its capability JSON omits device_index, device_pci_bdf, output_fp16 and source_expert_ids present in the current C++ Capability ABI.

Public NVFP4 API contract harness for capability, rejection ordering effects, single flight, split/fused boundary, compact residency, allocation stability, caller-sentinel preservation under optional injected poison and idempotent shutdown.

Opt-in int4 qualification and bounded-memory CPU differential oracle. Covers exact embedded source-ID map, compact-route rejection, split result, skipped-route zero, partition additivity, timing and RSS. Present source but absent from the Phase-1 Makefile targets.

Low-level legacy NVFP4/QuixiCore numerical and timing harness that bypasses B70Provider. It models no provider lifecycle; its direct device finder accepts B70 or Arc names, unlike select_b70's Intel+B70 rule.
Referenced grouped-prefill operation. The provider model retains acceptance/fallback and output ownership but delegates permutation and compute semantics to the compute branch.

Embedded native operation declarations called by the provider. Numerical/kernel internals are delegated to the compute and Quixi runtime models; this model retains family selection and completion effects.

assumptions: The finite model uses generation 7, batches up to 128, two abstract baked progress units and cumulative allocation counts; these bounds expose lifecycle behavior and are not production geometry claims.
A successful load action summarizes all source validation, device selection, persistent allocation and synchronous/asynchronous upload checks; rejectLoad summarizes fail-closed cleanup.
Tensor values and device commands are abstract, but compact-ID/finite-route validation, M thresholds, exact pending identity, output publication and caller-buffer preservation remain observable.

The model records Grouped and Int4Split as distinct selected kernels even though DispatchResult::kernel currently reports only split versus fused; this makes an implementation branch explicit without claiming the wire distinguishes it.
Native CS completion is atomic in the provider model; detailed Level Zero wait/write, marker and replay ordering belongs to command_streamer.ryu.

A classic dispatch error poisons only that pending result and does not permanently disable the provider. cs_failed and baked_disable are sticky for native modes, while classic issue/take remains an available fallback.
Registered host memory remains caller-owned and alive until provider use ends; the provider owns only the context registration and releases it on shutdown.
No result from a hardware-backed harness is asserted by this map; required banks, reference files, SYCL runtime and B70 hardware are external prerequisites.

implementation_checks.description: Run the existing int4 chain harness on qualified hardware to compare the provider's M=1 top-8 output with the one-record-at-a-time CPU dequant/SwiGLU/down-projection oracle; inspect the 5e-5 peak-relative bound, 5e-6 partition bound and exact all-skipped zero result.

Inspect or execute the existing API harness to confirm rejected generation/layer/compact IDs do not claim pending state, a second issue is busy, stale takes preserve pending identity, and the exact take retires it.
With SHOOTING_BRAKE_ENABLE_TEST_FAULTS, execute the sequence-bound post-kernel fault case and compare caller output plus DispatchResult sentinels before/after wrong-identity and exact poisoned takes.
Compare provider outputs with the frozen CPU-generated golden at M 1,2,4,8,16,32,128 to cover the split/fused boundary using tolerance 1e-6 + 1e-2*abs(expected).

Source-inspect serialized fields against Capability in b70_provider.hpp; verify that output_fp16 and the newer device/source-map fields are not present in this executable's JSON and therefore cannot be used as its wire-width query.
Source-inspect all returns before the final memcpy: wrong identity and short buffer preserve pending state, pending/async device error retires state, and no failing path writes caller output.

Source-inspect release_resources_locked ordering: native/copy queues drain before buffer frees, imported ranges release while context exists, mappings/fds close, pending identity clears, and cumulative allocation telemetry is not decremented.
